title: Development of Several Workflows for the Cryo-FIB/TEM
content: Cryo transmission electron microscopy (TEM) provides structural information of biological macromolecules close to their natural state without any disturbance during the sample preparation process. Recently, cryo TEM can achieve high resolution results in combination with the methods of single particle analysis (SPA) and cryo electron tomography (cryo-ET) [1]. Especially, cryo-ET is widely known as a well-established technique for analyzing the structural details of macromolecular complexes and organelles in the cells. Cryo-ET usually handle with thicker samples than those for SPA because the target of cryo-ET is mainly cells while the target of SPA is mainly purified protein particles. Quite recently, the desire to analyze macromolecular complexes within their cellular context has been increasing. It requires the ability to produce thin specimens from thick cells or tissues suitable for cryo-TEM. Cryo-FIB are rapidly evolving as a tool for preparing thin specimens for this purpose [2].
